title: The Gerund and Gerundive
subtitle: ars scrībendī. Carthāgō dēlenda est. Verbal nouns and adjectives of obligation.
objectives: Form the gerund (verbal noun) from any verb.
Form the gerundive (verbal adjective) from any verb.
Translate gerundive as 'must be X-ed' or 'to be X-ed'.

sections.heading: Gerund and gerundive
sections.body:
Gerund (verbal noun): present stem + -ndī, -ndō, -ndum, -ndō (gen., dat., acc., abl.):
  ars scrībendī — the art of writing
  cupidus vīdendī — desirous of seeing

Gerundive (verbal adjective): present stem + -ndus, -a, -um:
  Carthāgō dēlenda est. — Carthage must be destroyed.
  līber legendus — a book to be read

Cicero writes: vīvendī causa. — For the sake of living.
Cato writes: Carthāgō dēlenda est. — Carthage must be destroyed.

items.answer: dūcendus, dūcenda, dūcendum — to be led
